elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice to HDI." The element is disjunctive and this hosting agreement has no Order Forms, so the Agreement-level right suffices.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The Company's new right runs on "ninety (90) days' prior written notice", not 30 days. To reach preferred the notice figure in the inserted sentence would have to read thirty (30) days.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund obligation appears anywhere in the rendered language. The drafter asserts no prepaid fees exist under the Section 3.1 revenue-share model, but Section 3.1 is not in the supplied record, so the inapplicability of the condition cannot be verified.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 renewal limb now reads "unless terminated by HDI for convenience, only at the end of a term, upon ninety (90) days written notice to the Company", so HDI cannot end the Agreement for convenience mid-term; the qualifier "for convenience" leaves HDI's cause rights (e.g. Section 1.6) intact.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Operation 2 inserts a standalone Company right: "The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice to HDI" — 90 days sits at the top of the 60–90 day band. The failing deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" is contradicted by the rendered text and appears keyed to the preferred 30-day formulation rather than to substantive absence.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) now reads "the lesser of (i) the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, divided by two, and (ii) the payments due to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date", so prong (ii) operates as a three-month fee ceiling on the Termination Payment.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The renewal limb expressly confines HDI to convenience termination "only at the end of a term"; the surviving "Such notice shall specify the date..." mechanic is subordinate to that express limitation and does not licence a mid-term date for HDI.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: HDI's convenience limb retains "upon ninety (90) days written notice to the Company", and the rewrite cures the dangling "to the other" antecedent left by deleting the symmetric "either Party" formulation.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: all four fallback elements are met in operative language (Company convenience right at 90 days; three-month fee ceiling as prong (ii) of a "lesser of"; HDI confined to end-of-term convenience termination on 90 days' notice to the Company).

The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" reports false, but inspection of the rendered text shows the right is expressly granted to the Company (a listed customer alias) for convenience on 90 days' notice. The check appears calibrated to the preferred 30-day pattern; it is not evidence of a substantive gap, and the three operation-application checks and the coverage/minimality gates all pass.

Preferred is correctly not claimed: notice remains 90 rather than 30 days, and no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund is added (the record does not include Section 3.1, so the "no prepaid fees" premise is asserted rather than verifiable).

Minimal: each of the three operations maps to a distinct fallback element with no duplication — the Company's right is moved out of the passive "either Party" limb into its own sentence rather than stated twice — and the favourable existing mechanics are retained (the $800,000 deduction and divide-by-two computation survive as prong (i), and 4.2(b) netting, 4.2(c) quarterly instalments, the one-year term and the renewal structure are untouched). Nothing outside the checklist is imported; the breach carve-out to 4.2(a) is properly reserved to the breach/remedies rule rather than double-counted here.

Non-blocking drafting repair to tighten before sending: because the renewal limb was narrowed to HDI, the defined term "Termination Date" in "Such notice shall specify the date..." now attaches only to HDI's notice, while Sections 4.2(a) prongs (i) and (ii) and 4.2(c) compute off the Termination Date on a Company termination. Add ", which notice shall specify the Termination Date," to the inserted Company sentence (or revert "Such notice" to cover notices given by either Party) so the payment computation and instalment start date remain determinate.

Assessment is limited to the supplied excerpts; if any other provision confers a separate HDI convenience or at-will exit right, the "only at the end of a term" limitation should be extended there as well so the fallback constraint is not undercut elsewhere.
